Hi, I'm Antony, an undergraduate studying mathematics. This is where I write up the maths I enjoy most: proofs I keep coming back to, problems I've been stuck on, and the occasional picture that explains more than a page of algebra.

## What I'm into

**Number theory.** Primes, congruences, and the strange patterns they leave behind, like the diagonals in the [Ulam spiral](posts/ulam-diagonals/) at the top of the home page.

**Analysis.** Series, limits, and why $\pi$ keeps showing up in places it seems to have no business being.

**Combinatorics and olympiad problems.** Short problems where one good idea makes everything fall into place.

## About this site

Longer pieces live under [Writing](archive.qmd), quick ones in the [Notebook](notebook.qmd), and problems to try (with hints) under [Problems](problems.qmd). Every definition and theorem from every post is collected on the [Theorems](theorems.qmd) page.

The picture is a dragon curve. Fold a strip of paper in half eight times, always in the same direction, then open it out so every crease makes a right angle: this is the shape you get. The curve never crosses itself, and four copies turned about a common point fit together to cover the whole plane.
